# What Is a Good SHSAT Score? 2026 Cutoffs, Targets by School


### TLDR


A good SHSAT score depends on which New York City Specialized High School a student wants to attend. For 2026 admissions, the lowest qualifying scores for 9th-grade entry ranged from 495 at The Brooklyn Latin School to 561 at Stuyvesant High School. Students preparing for the fall 2026 SHSAT should use these results as historical benchmarks, aim above their target school's previous cutoff, and avoid treating any practice-score estimate as a guarantee of admission.


> **What Is a Good SHSAT Score? (Quick Answer)**
>
>
> A good SHSAT score is a composite score that makes a student competitive for one or more of the eight testing Specialized High Schools in New York City. For 2026 admissions, a score of 520 would have cleared several schools, while Stuyvesant required 561 for 9th-grade entry. A practical preparation goal is to score 10–20 points above the most recent cutoff for a target school, although a larger buffer may be appropriate because future cutoffs can change.
>
>
> **Important for fall 2026 test-takers:** The fall 2026 SHSAT is for September 2027 admission. The 2026 cutoff scores below describe the previous admissions cycle; they are not the cutoffs for students taking the test this fall.


For 2026 admissions, the[9th-grade-entry cutoffs](https://www.schools.nyc.gov/enrollment/enroll-grade-by-grade/specialized-high-schools) ranged from 495 to 561. That means a 500 was technically above the Brooklyn Latin cutoff but below the other seven schools. A 540 cleared most schools but fell short of Stuyvesant. Context matters more than the number itself.


Not sure where you stand?[Start a practice session](https://miyagilabs.ai/learn) to identify your baseline and the skills costing you points.


## Quick Score Benchmarks


Here is a practical framework for what counts as a good SHSAT score, based on 2026 admissions data:


-


**Around 500:** In the historical offer range for the lowest-cutoff school only. Very little cushion.


-


**520+:** Clears several schools including Brooklyn Tech, HSAS, and Staten Island Tech in 2026.


-


**540+:** Competitive for higher-cutoff schools like HSMSE and Queens Science.


-


**561+:** Stuyvesant range in 2026.


-


**565 to 580+:** A stronger Stuyvesant planning target with buffer for year-to-year movement.


These are planning ranges, not future guarantees. Cutoffs change annually because they depend on the applicant pool, the school rankings students submit, and available seats.

## What SHSAT Score Should You Aim For?


Your SHSAT target should depend on your preferred schools, your current practice performance, and how much improvement you can realistically make before test day. The most recent cutoff is a useful reference point, but it should not be treated as a guaranteed admission score.


A reasonable starting strategy is to set a practice-score goal 10–20 points above a school's latest published cutoff. For highly competitive targets, or when practice scores fluctuate considerably, consider aiming higher.


### If Your Goal Is to Get Into a Specialized High School


Start by identifying several schools you would genuinely be happy to attend. Brooklyn Latin had the lowest 9th-grade-entry cutoff in the 2026 cycle, at 495. A practice goal around 510–520 gives a buffer above that historical result and places more schools within reach based on the previous cycle's data.


This is a preparation strategy, not a promise that a particular score will secure an offer.


### If Brooklyn Tech Is Your First Choice


Brooklyn Tech's 2026 9th-grade-entry cutoff was 506. A practice target of 520 or higher would put you above that historical result by 14 points or more. Continue tracking your results across multiple timed practice sessions rather than relying on one high score.


### If You Are Targeting Bronx Science, Queens Science, or HSMSE


The 2026 cutoffs were 525 for Bronx Science, 531 for Queens Science, and 539 for HSMSE. A practice goal in the 540–550 range would sit above all three historical cutoffs. Future cutoffs may differ, so use this range as a study goal rather than a prediction.


### If Stuyvesant Is Your First Choice


Stuyvesant's 2026 9th-grade-entry cutoff was 561. A practice target around 575 or higher would give you a larger buffer against that historical result. It would not guarantee admission, and the actual cutoff for the next cycle will not be known until offers are released.


The most useful target is one you can monitor over time. Compare multiple practice attempts, review mistakes, and update your plan as your accuracy and timing improve.


## How SHSAT Cutoffs Actually Work


Understanding how cutoffs are determined changes how you interpret a good SHSAT score. Here is the process, step by step:


1.


Students take the SHSAT.


2.


NYC Public Schools converts each student’s performance into scaled ELA and Math scores.


3.


Those two scaled scores are added into a composite used for rank ordering.


4.


Students are processed in descending composite score order.


5.


When a student’s turn arrives, the system checks their ranked school list.


6.


The student receives an offer to the highest-ranked school that still has an available seat.


7.


A school’s cutoff becomes the score of the last student to receive a seat.


This means cutoffs are retroactive, not preset. Practitioners on Reddit explain this clearly: families sometimes think cutoffs are arbitrary numbers decided before admissions, but they are actually the[final lowest admitted scores](https://www.reddit.com/r/SHSAT/comments/1rv716l/ranking_schools_scores/) after seats are filled. If a student does not get an offer, it is because all seats at every school they listed were filled by students with higher scores.


One more thing worth noting: students are only considered for schools they listed. If you leave a school off your SHSAT registration, you will not be considered for it regardless of your score. NYC Public Schools[advises families to list choices](https://www.schools.nyc.gov/enrollment/enroll-grade-by-grade/how-students-get-offers-to-doe-public-schools) in true preference order. Ranking a lower-cutoff school first does not make you “safer.”


Here is a simple example. If you rank Stuyvesant first and Brooklyn Tech second, and your score is too low for Stuyvesant when your turn comes but high enough for Brooklyn Tech, you receive Brooklyn Tech. You do not lose your Brooklyn Tech chance by ranking Stuyvesant higher.


## Why Last Year’s Cutoff Is Not a Guarantee


This point is worth repeating because it is the most common source of false confidence. Cutoffs change every year for several reasons:


**Applicant pool size varies.** In the most recent cycle, approximately 26,100 8th graders took the SHSAT and about[4,000 received offers](https://infohub.nyced.org/docs/default-source/default-document-library/ose/omnibus-admissions-dr-2026.pdf) , a roughly 15.4% offer rate. If more or fewer students test next year, or if the pool is stronger or weaker, cutoffs move.


**Ranking behavior shifts.** If more students rank a particular school first, its cutoff can rise even if the overall pool stays the same size.


**Seat availability changes.** Smaller schools are more volatile because a handful of seats can swing the cutoff significantly.


**The test itself is changing.** Beginning in fall 2026, the SHSAT is computer-adaptive, with 50 ELA questions and 50 Math questions over 180 minutes. The system adjusts question difficulty based on the student’s responses. This means raw-question-count score calculators are less reliable, and 2027 cutoffs could look different from prior years.


The bottom line: use prior cutoffs for planning, not as promises. Add a buffer of at least 10 to 20 points above your target school’s most recent cutoff. If you want less risk, aim 25 to 30+ points above.


## How the Computer-Adaptive SHSAT Changes Score Planning in 2026


Beginning in fall 2026, the SHSAT will be administered as a computer-adaptive test. This means the testing system adjusts question difficulty as a student answers questions, using the pattern of responses to estimate performance.


### What Students Need to Know


-


**The test has two sections:** English Language Arts (ELA) and Mathematics, with 50 questions per section.


-


**Standard testing time is 180 minutes:** Students should practice managing their time across both sections.


-


**Question difficulty adapts:** The testing system uses responses and item difficulty to estimate performance as the exam progresses.


-


**Official scores are not simple raw totals:** NYC Public Schools transforms performance scores into scaled subtest scores, which are then added to produce the composite score used for admissions ranking.


-


**Old score calculators may be unreliable:** A raw number of correct answers cannot be assumed to translate directly into an official composite score under the new adaptive format.


### How Should Students Prepare?


Use the official digital practice materials to become familiar with the testing interface and question types. Track your accuracy by topic, review explanations for missed questions, and monitor pacing across full-length practice sessions.


When reviewing practice results, distinguish between an official score, a third-party estimate, and your raw accuracy. These are different measurements and should not be treated as interchangeable.


Historical cutoffs remain useful for setting goals, but the 2026 test format makes it particularly important to avoid presenting unofficial score conversions as guaranteed predictions of admission.


## What Is a Good Practice-Test Score?


A good practice-test score is one that consistently lands above your target school’s recent cutoff under realistic timing conditions. A single high score on one practice test is far less meaningful than a pattern of results across multiple tests.


There are important caveats. Practice-test scores are not official SHSAT scores. The fall 2026 SHSAT is computer-adaptive, so raw correct answers do not translate cleanly into an official composite. And score calculators should be treated as rough estimates at best.


Practitioners on Reddit warn that SHSAT score calculators can be[“all over the place”](https://www.reddit.com/r/SHSAT/comments/1j96blg) and can create false confidence. The advice that comes up repeatedly in community threads is to track raw accuracy by topic, monitor pacing, review repeated mistakes, and focus on official practice-test performance rather than trusting one converted composite estimate. For a broader look at how prediction tools work across standardized tests, see how[score predictors function](https://miyagilabs.ai/sat/score-predictors) and the assumptions behind them.


When evaluating your practice-test performance, focus on these factors:


-


Was the test timed realistically (180 minutes total)?


-


What was the source of the questions? Official NYC Public Schools practice materials are more reliable than third-party sets.


-


Which ELA and Math topics did you miss repeatedly?


-


Did you finish both sections, or did pacing cost you questions?


-


For the current adaptive test, did you practice on a screen-based interface? The format is now part of readiness.


A score that barely clears a cutoff on one practice test is not a reliable indicator. A score that clears the cutoff on three or four different practice tests, with consistent section performance, tells you much more. Understanding how[full-length practice exams](https://miyagilabs.ai/sat/practice-tests) build test-day readiness applies across standardized tests, not just the SHSAT.

The takeaway is simple. If you are a first-time 9th grader, use the 10th-grade-entry table and plan for higher targets.

More practice tests automatically mean better results.

## What Is the SHSAT Discovery Program?


The SHSAT Discovery Program provides an additional admissions pathway for eligible students who meet the program's criteria. It is intended for students from qualifying educational and economic backgrounds who score below the applicable SHSAT cutoff.


Eligibility is not determined by a student's score alone. Students and families should review the current NYC Public Schools Discovery Program rules, including eligibility requirements, school participation, and application procedures.


Do not assume that every student who scores below a school's cutoff qualifies. A below-cutoff score also does not automatically mean that a student will receive a Discovery offer.


**What should families do?** Check the official Discovery Program guidance for the relevant admissions cycle and speak with the student's school counselor or NYC Public Schools if eligibility is unclear.


## How to Improve Toward Your Target SHSAT Score


Knowing what a good SHSAT score is does nothing unless you have a plan to reach it. Here is a framework that works.


**Step 1: Take a diagnostic.** You need a baseline before you can set a realistic target. A timed diagnostic under test-like conditions tells you where you stand today, not where you hope to be. To see how baseline assessments work in practice,[take a diagnostic test](https://miyagilabs.ai/sat/diagnostic-test) and compare the concept to your SHSAT prep.


**Step 2: Identify your weakest skills.** The SHSAT tests specific ELA and Math skills. A diagnostic should show you which question types and topics are costing you the most points. Focus there first.


**Step 3: Practice with purpose.** Random practice is inefficient. Targeted practice on weak areas, followed by review and re-testing, is how scores actually move. Track which errors repeat and which ones you have eliminated.


**Step 4: Take full-length timed tests regularly.** Pacing matters as much as knowledge. The SHSAT gives you 180 minutes for 100 questions. Running out of time on test day is avoidable if you practice under realistic constraints.


**Step 5: Prepare for the digital interface.** The fall 2026 SHSAT is computer-adaptive and screen-based. Paper-only practice leaves a gap. Students should practice navigating questions, reviewing flagged items, and managing time on a screen.


**Step 6: Re-assess and adjust.** After a few weeks of targeted practice, take another full-length test. Compare your section scores, pacing, and error patterns to your baseline. Adjust your plan accordingly. Students who follow this cycle consistently see[measurable score improvement](https://miyagilabs.ai/results) over time.


The concept of “good” is personal. For one family, getting into any specialized high school is the goal. For another, only Stuyvesant will do. Either way, the path is the same: diagnose, practice weak areas, test under realistic conditions, review, and repeat.


## FAQ


### What is a good SHSAT score?


A good SHSAT score is high enough to earn an offer to a specialized high school on your ranked list. For 2026 admissions, 9th-grade-entry cutoffs ranged from 495 at Brooklyn Latin to 561 at Stuyvesant. A practical target should be above the most recent cutoff for your target school, not exactly at it, because cutoffs shift every year.


### Is 500 a good SHSAT score?


A 500 was above Brooklyn Latin’s 2026 cutoff of 495 but below the cutoffs for Brooklyn Tech (506), HSAS (507), Staten Island Tech (517), Bronx Science (525), Queens Science (531), HSMSE (539), and Stuyvesant (561). It is a meaningful score but not a strong all-school score.


### Is 520 a good SHSAT score?


A 520 would have cleared Brooklyn Latin, Brooklyn Tech, HSAS, and Staten Island Tech in 2026. It was below Bronx Science (525), Queens Science (531), HSMSE (539), and Stuyvesant (561). It is a strong target for several schools but not competitive for every specialized high school.


### What SHSAT score do you need for Brooklyn Tech?


Brooklyn Tech’s 2026 9th-grade-entry cutoff was 506. A planning target of 520 or above gives more cushion because cutoffs change year to year and a score exactly at last year’s cutoff means you were the last student admitted.


### What SHSAT score do you need for Stuyvesant?


Stuyvesant’s 2026 cutoff was 561. A realistic planning target is 565 to 580 or above, because the cutoff has ranged from 556 to 566 in recent years and landing exactly at the cutoff carries significant risk.


### Do SHSAT cutoffs change every year?


Yes. Cutoffs depend on the number of test-takers, the strength of the applicant pool, how students rank schools, and available seats. Historical data from 2020 to 2026 shows movement at every specialized high school.


### Should I trust an SHSAT score calculator?


Use calculators as rough ballparks only. Official SHSAT scoring transforms performance into scaled section scores, and the fall 2026 adaptive format makes raw-to-scaled conversions less predictable. Track section performance, pacing, and error patterns instead of fixating on one converted number.


### Does ranking a specialized high school lower hurt my chances?


No. NYC Public Schools processes students by score, then checks their ranked list. Rank schools in true preference order. You are only considered for schools you listed, so leaving a school off your registration means you cannot receive an offer there, but ranking it second or third does not reduce your chances if your score qualifies.
